Causal masks block future positions; they do not exclude padding. PyTorch’s `key_padding_mask` excludes padded keys/values, but does not zero padded query outputs. Zero embeddings alone still permit attention mass on padding; biases and subsequent layers can produce nonzero states. Implementation matters: original SASRec explicitly masks keys and intermediate padded states; current pmixer code supplies only a causal mask. Both score the final array position, not automatically the last nonpadding interaction. [PyTorch documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.MultiheadAttention), [original SASRec](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/modules.py), [pmixer implementation](https://github.com/pmixer/SASRec.pytorch/blob/master/python/model.py).

Consequently, interior padding and deletion/repacking are different interventions. Padding preserves surviving items’ absolute positions but introduces holes potentially absent during training. Deletion followed by right-aligned repacking changes some survivors’ position embeddings while preserving order: `[a,b,c,d] → [0,a,c,d]` shifts `a`, whereas `[a,0,c,d]` preserves its index. Removing the final interaction without repacking also changes the scored query into padding. These are deductions from the implementations, not evidence of temporal dependence. [SASRec position embeddings and final-position scoring](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py).

Recommended controls: compare equal-count recent versus older removals; substitute real items at fixed positions to probe content without holes; compare hole masking against repacking with original position IDs retained, then against ordinary reindexed repacking. With correctly excluded padding, preserved position IDs, identical surviving order/readout, and dropout disabled, holes and packing should closely agree—use this as an implementation check. Keep candidates fixed, verify finite outputs and padded-key exclusion, and separately test final-item removal. Report paired score/rank changes; agreement across controls supports recency sensitivity, while disagreement exposes position or masking artifacts.
